rationale: Adopt @lottiefiles/dotlottie-react 0.21.1 with its required runtime @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web 0.82.1. It is the only React option that combines an active release line, MIT licensing, npm provenance, React 17/18/19 support, both Lottie JSON and .lottie support, and a self-hostable WASM/worker runtime. The React 19 spike loaded .lottie and JSON side by side from a self-hosted WASM file in 58 ms, with 90 frames each and no page errors. The JS bundle was 356.93 KB / 93.15 KB gzip, plus a 481 KB gzip WASM. lottie-react is a clean active wrapper but sits on lottie-web 5.13.0, which has not shipped since May 2025 and contains eval; it is held as a JSON-only legacy fallback. lottie-web itself is held for the same maintenance and CSP reasons. The archived LottieFiles players, the deprecated @dotlottie/react-player and the stale react-lottie wrapper are rejected; @dotlottie/react-player also pulls sharp with an install script and LGPL libvips. @lottiefiles/dotlottie-wc is a viable non-React fallback but is held because it adds lit and is not React-first.
scope: Library selection for React DOM Lottie playback. Animation assets, authoring, CDN choice, React Native and application-specific CSP are consumer obligations.
criteria: Permissive license across the full dependency tree
React 18 and 19 supported when a React wrapper is used
Browser playback; SSR is optional and client-only is acceptable
Actively maintained: a release within 12 months across the chosen runtime stack
No unfixed high or critical advisories
No install scripts in the dependency tree
Runtime assets such as WASM or workers must be self-hostable; no mandatory CDN dependency
If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap

alternatives_considered.name: @lottiefiles/dotlottie-react 0.21.1
alternatives_considered.reason: Active, MIT, provenance-signed, React 17/18/19, supports .lottie and JSON, self-hostable WASM/worker, clean install and no advisories. React 19 spike passed.

alternatives_considered.name: @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web 0.82.1
alternatives_considered.reason: The exact runtime dependency beneath the React wrapper; active, MIT, provenance-signed, dependency-free and self-hostable.

alternatives_considered.name: lottie-react 3.1.2
alternatives_considered.reason: Active wrapper and good types, but it depends on stale lottie-web 5.13.0, is JSON-only, has no provenance and inherits lottie-web's eval usage.

alternatives_considered.name: lottie-web 5.13.0
alternatives_considered.reason: The long-standing JSON renderer is MIT, fast and dependency-free, but has no release since May 2025, no .lottie support, no provenance and contains eval.

alternatives_considered.name: @lottiefiles/dotlottie-wc 0.11.1
alternatives_considered.reason: Active, MIT and provenance-signed, but a web component that adds lit and is not React-first. Use only as a fallback behind a React wrapper.

alternatives_considered.name: @lottiefiles/react-lottie-player 3.6.0
alternatives_considered.reason: Deprecated in its README, repository archived, last release January 2025, and still tied to lottie-web.

alternatives_considered.name: @lottiefiles/lottie-player 2.0.12
alternatives_considered.reason: Archived web component, last release November 2024, five runtime dependencies and no release within 12 months.

alternatives_considered.name: react-lottie 1.2.10
alternatives_considered.reason: Stale wrapper, no types, no provenance, and babel-runtime brings core-js 2 with a postinstall script.

alternatives_considered.name: @dotlottie/react-player 1.6.19
alternatives_considered.reason: Deprecated, peer stops at React 18, 76 MB installed, sharp install script and LGPL libvips in the tree.

alternatives_considered.name: lottie-react-native 7.5.0
alternatives_considered.reason: The requirement is React DOM, not React Native.

alternatives_considered.name: @lottiefiles/lottie-interactivity 1.6.2
alternatives_considered.reason: An optional interaction layer, not a player. It has not shipped since 2023 and is not needed for basic playback.

conditions: Self-host dotlottie-player.wasm and dotlottie.worker.js from the installed package, or explicitly accept the version-pinned jsDelivr/unpkg fallback.
Call setWasmUrl() before constructing players. Use setWorkerUrl() and DotLottieWorkerReact if the worker path is used.
Use the component in a client-only boundary; do not server-render it.
Verify the consuming application's CSP allows WebAssembly and, if used, the worker. Record whether wasm-unsafe-eval and worker-src are required.
Use DotLottieWorkerReact for heavy or multiple animations; keep the main-thread player for simple cases.
Test both .lottie and JSON assets, including the actual asset sizes and any state machines or themes in use.
Do not use lottie-web or lottie-react for new work unless a legacy JSON dependency requires them; pin 5.13.0 / 3.1.2 and record the provenance gap if so.
unknowns: React 18 was not spiked; the peer range covers it, but the consuming application should verify React 18 if used.
The spike used a simple 90-frame animation. State machines, themes, audio, worker rendering and very large .lottie files were not exercised.
The exact CSP cost (wasm-unsafe-eval and worker-src) depends on the consuming application's policy.
The WASM runtime is about 481 KB gzip; its real-world cache and first-frame cost depend on hosting and network.
The .lottie assets and their licensing are consumer obligations; the player licence does not grant rights to arbitrary animation assets.
reversal_cost: Low to moderate: @lottiefiles/dotlottie-react is a small React wrapper, but switching to lottie-react means changing the player component and accepting the stale lottie-web runtime. The asset format should remain portable.
review_triggers: A new high or critical advisory affects @lottiefiles/dotlottie-react or @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web.
The DotLottie React or web package stops releasing within 12 months.
The WASM or worker URL contract changes, or self-hosting stops being supported.
The React peer range drops React 18 or 19.
The licence of the React wrapper or web player changes.
lottie-web resumes releases or fixes its eval/CSP issue and becomes a viable JSON-only alternative.
A maintained React wrapper for .lottie appears with a better footprint.
